title: What should you do in the 30 minutes before a case interview?
description: A calm 30-minute routine for the half hour before your interview: familiar reading, a speech warm-up, one short mock and time to settle.
hook: The half hour before an interview matters more than people think. Here is a calm warm-up that gets your head and voice ready without cramming.
body:
1. 10 minutes: familiar reading. Skim a book such as Blitzscaling or your own vocabulary notes. Look for ideas you already understand, not new jargon.
  2. 5 minutes: speech warm-up. Do a short routine on SpeechOn.app (free) or read one paragraph aloud. Practise clear articulation and a natural pace.
  3. 10 minutes: one short mock. Recap a prompt, outline three useful branches and deliver a 60-second recommendation. Focus on one improvement.
  4. 5 minutes: settle in. Check your materials, breathe normally and avoid introducing a new framework. Being rested matters more than cramming.

What not to do

Do not learn a new framework now, and do not do a full hard case. You want to arrive warm and confident, not tired and full of half-remembered lists. Being rested matters more than one extra hour of practice.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation.
